trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Disney World, Orlando, Florida
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway - Free Theme Park Shuttle
hotel.location: 7470 W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy, Kissimmee, US (28.3314,-81.5863)

day_by_day.morning: No activities - flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities - flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Orlando International Airport at 22:30 via United Airlines. Collect luggage, take the free hotel shuttle from the airport to Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway. Check in, unpack, and review your Disney World park tickets and plans for the week. Download the My Disney Experience app if not already done.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport food before departure
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport terminal food
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite at a 24-hour McDonald's or Denny's near the hotel on W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy (within 1 mile of hotel) — budget around $8–$12 per person

day_by_day.notes: Keep energy light tonight — big days ahead. Pick up snacks and water bottles at a nearby Walmart Supercenter (3.5 miles away on W Irlo Bronson) to save money on park drinks throughout the week. Set alarms early for Day 2. Confirm free shuttle schedule to Magic Kingdom at the hotel front desk.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and take the free hotel shuttle to Magic Kingdom — aim to arrive at park opening (typically 9:00 AM). Head straight to Tomorrowland for Space Mountain and Buzz Lightyear's Space Ranger Spin before crowds build. Then walk through Fantasyland to ride Seven Dwarfs Mine Train and Peter Pan's Flight using Lightning Lane if budget allows, or queue early. Explore Cinderella Castle and grab a photo.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, head to Adventureland for Pirates of the Caribbean and the Jungle Cruise. Visit Liberty Square for the Haunted Mansion. Take a mid-afternoon break at the hotel (use the free shuttle) to rest and cool off — this saves money on park food and avoids peak heat and crowds from 2–4 PM.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Magic Kingdom via shuttle for the evening. Enjoy Frontierland's Big Thunder Mountain Railroad and watch the spectacular Magic Kingdom Fireworks (Happily Ever After) at park close. Soak in the Main Street USA atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat breakfast at the hotel or use snacks purchased from Walmart — granola bars, fruit, and juice to save $10–$15 per person
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House in Liberty Square — budget-friendly counter service with fish and chips or chicken strips around $12–$15 per person
meals.dinner: Pecos Bill Tall Tale Inn & Cafe in Frontierland — hearty burgers and nachos around $13–$16 per person; use the free toppings bar to bulk up your meal

day_by_day.notes: Bring refillable water bottles — free ice water is available at any quick-service location. Wear comfortable shoes and apply sunscreen. June weather in Orlando is hot and humid (90°F+) with afternoon thunderstorms likely — pack a small poncho. Purchase a Disney Dining Plan or use mobile order on the app to save time.

day_by_day.morning: Take the free hotel shuttle to EPCOT, arriving at rope drop (typically 9:00 AM). Head immediately to World Discovery for Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (virtual queue — join as soon as the park opens via the app). Then ride Test Track and Mission: SPACE (Green Mission for a family-friendly option). Explore the stunning EPCOT Geodesphere and Spaceship Earth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through World Showcase — explore the pavilions of Mexico, Norway (ride Frozen Ever After!), China, Germany, Italy, America, Japan, Morocco, France, United Kingdom, and Canada. Enjoy free cultural entertainment, street performers, and architecture. This is a great low-cost way to 'travel the world' without spending extra.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for EPCOT's nighttime spectacular — Luminous The Symphony of Us — a stunning fireworks and water show over World Showcase Lagoon. Free with park admission and a magical end to the day.

meals.breakfast: Hotel snacks or granola bars from Walmart stash
meals.lunch: Sunshine Seasons in The Land pavilion — one of EPCOT's best budget counter-service spots with rotating seasonal dishes, sandwiches, and grain bowls around $12–$14 per person
meals.dinner: Yorkshire County Fish Shop in the UK Pavilion — fish and chips for around $10–$13 per person, one of EPCOT's most affordable and delicious quick-service options

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT is very walkable but large — wear comfortable shoes. The World Showcase doesn't open until 11:00 AM, so plan Future World/World Discovery first. Many World Showcase pavilions offer free entertainment and cultural experiences. Avoid expensive sit-down restaurants in World Showcase — they can run $40–$80 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Take the free hotel shuttle to Hollywood Studios, arriving at rope drop (typically 9:00 AM). Rush immediately to Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge — join the virtual queue or Lightning Lane for Rise of the Resistance, one of Disney's most immersive rides. Then ride Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run. Explore the incredible Star Wars land atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Toy Story Land for Slinky Dog Dash and Toy Story Mania. Then visit Sunset Boulevard for Rock 'n' Roller Coaster and The Twilight Zone Tower of Terror — two of Disney's most thrilling rides. Take a mid-afternoon break at the hotel if needed to avoid peak heat.
day_by_day.evening: Return for the evening to catch the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular (check show times). End the night with Fantasmic! — a spectacular outdoor nighttime show featuring Mickey Mouse, Disney villains, and fireworks on the lagoon. Arrive 45–60 minutes early for good seating.

meals.breakfast: Hotel snacks — fruit, granola bars, and water from your Walmart supply
meals.lunch: Woody's Lunch Box in Toy Story Land — fun theming with grilled cheese sandwiches and totchos (tater tot nachos) for around $10–$13 per person
meals.dinner: ABC Commissary near Echo Lake — burgers, wraps, and international dishes for around $12–$15 per person; one of the park's most affordable counter-service spots

day_by_day.notes: Hollywood Studios is the most ride-dense park — plan Lightning Lane Multi Pass for Rise of the Resistance if budget allows (around $20–$30 per person extra). Fantasmic! dining packages exist but are pricey — arrive early for free seating instead. Check the My Disney Experience app for live wait times throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Take the free hotel shuttle to Animal Kingdom, arriving at rope drop (typically 8:00 AM — often opens earlier than other parks). Head straight to Pandora – The World of Avatar for Flight of Passage (the park's most popular ride — waits can exceed 2 hours by 9 AM). Then ride Na'vi River Journey for a beautiful, relaxing boat experience through bioluminescent rainforest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Africa — take the Kilimanjaro Safaris for an incredible free-roaming animal experience (best in the morning or late afternoon when animals are most active — consider a second ride now). Walk the Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail. Head to Asia for Expedition Everest and Kali River Rapids (you WILL get wet — great for the heat!).
day_by_day.evening: Catch the Rivers of Light nighttime spectacular if running (check schedule). Explore Discovery Island and the iconic Tree of Life — look for the hidden animal carvings. Animal Kingdom typically closes earlier than other parks, so head back to the hotel for a relaxing evening by the pool.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite at Zuri's Swamped Snacks near the park entrance — Mickey waffles or pastries for around $6–$8
meals.lunch: Flame Tree Barbecue in Discovery Island — one of Disney's best counter-service meals with smoked ribs, pulled pork, and chicken for around $14–$17 per person; beautiful outdoor waterfront seating
meals.dinner: Relax at the hotel — use your Walmart grocery supplies to make a simple meal in the room (sandwiches, fruit, chips) and save $30–$50 for the family. Or visit a nearby Kissimmee restaurant on W Irlo Bronson Hwy

day_by_day.notes: Animal Kingdom is best experienced in the morning — animals are more active and temperatures are cooler. Bring a change of clothes or a poncho for Kali River Rapids. The park often closes by 8–9 PM, making it the shortest park day — use the extra time to rest or explore the Kissimmee area near the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely morning! Have a relaxed breakfast at the hotel. Spend the morning at the Ramada hotel pool — a great free activity to recharge after four intense park days. Let the kids splash around while you plan the final day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the free hotel shuttle (or a short rideshare — about $10–$15) to Disney Springs — Disney's free-admission shopping, dining, and entertainment district. Explore the World of Disney store (largest Disney merchandise store in the world), browse unique shops, watch street performers, and enjoy the lively atmosphere along the waterfront. Visit the LEGO Store with its impressive outdoor LEGO sculptures.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner at Disney Springs and catch some live entertainment. Walk along the waterfront and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere. Head back to the hotel via shuttle or rideshare and pack for the final park day tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Walmart snacks — fruit, yogurt, cereal to save money
meals.lunch: D-Luxe Burger at Disney Springs — gourmet burgers with creative toppings for around $13–$16 per person; great quality for the price
meals.dinner: Blaze Fast-Fire'd Pizza at Disney Springs — build-your-own personal pizzas for around $10–$13 per person; one of the best budget options at Disney Springs

day_by_day.notes: Disney Springs admission is completely FREE — no park ticket required. This is a great budget day to rest legs and still enjoy Disney magic. The LEGO Store, World of Disney, and many other shops are free to browse. Avoid the sit-down restaurants at Disney Springs (The Boathouse, STK, etc.) as they are expensive — stick to counter service. Check for free live music performances on the waterfront stages.

day_by_day.morning: Final park day! Take the free hotel shuttle back to Magic Kingdom for a morning revisit. Use this day to ride anything you missed or loved from Day 2. Hit your favorite rides with shorter Sunday morning crowds. Grab a Mickey-shaped pretzel or Dole Whip as a classic Disney treat. Spend time on Main Street USA for last-minute souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back to the hotel by early afternoon (around 1–2 PM). Check out of the hotel (or store luggage at the front desk). Take a final dip in the hotel pool. Pack all belongings and organize souvenirs. Arrange transportation back to Orlando International Airport — confirm hotel shuttle schedule or book a rideshare (Uber/Lyft typically $25–$35 to MCO).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Orlando International Airport for your departure flight. Arrive at least 2 hours before domestic departure or 3 hours for international. Reflect on an amazing week at Disney World! Browse airport shops for any last-minute Florida or Disney souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Casey's Corner on Main Street USA, Magic Kingdom — hot dogs and breakfast items for around $8–$11; a classic Disney quick-service spot
meals.lunch: Cosmic Ray's Starlight Café in Tomorrowland — one of Magic Kingdom's largest and most affordable counter-service restaurants with burgers, chicken, and rotisserie options for around $12–$15 per person
meals.dinner: Airport dining at MCO — grab a meal at one of the terminal restaurants or fast food options before your flight; budget around $12–$18 per person

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time (usually 11 AM) — request a late checkout if your flight is in the evening. Use any remaining Disney gift cards or dining credits today. Take final photos at Magic Kingdom's iconic spots — Cinderella Castle, Main Street USA, and the park entrance. The free hotel shuttle to the airport may be available — confirm with the front desk the night before. Total estimated budget for 7 days (excluding flights and park tickets): $150–$250 per person for food using counter-service dining and Walmart grocery supplements.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30. No morning activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit. No afternoon activities scheduled.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Orlando International Airport at 22:30 via United Airlines flight UA. Collect luggage, arrange ground transportation (Mears Connect shuttle or rideshare ~$25–35) to Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway. Check in, unpack, and review the week's park plans. Pick up any essentials at the nearby Walmart Supercenter on W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy (open 24 hrs, ~5 min drive).

meals.breakfast: N/A – In transit
meals.lunch: N/A – In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night bite at Denny's (open 24 hrs, ~0.5 mi from hotel) or order delivery via DoorDash/Uber Eats to the hotel room. Budget ~$15–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — rest is essential before a full week of parks. Confirm free theme park shuttle schedule at the hotel front desk. Download the My Disney Experience app and link park tickets if not already done. Purchase park tickets in advance online to save time and money.

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom Park Adventure – Take the hotel's free theme park shuttle (departs ~8:00 AM; confirm schedule at front desk). Arrive at Magic Kingdom early for rope drop (~9:00 AM). Head straight to Tomorrowland for Space Mountain and Buzz Lightyear's Space Ranger Spin before crowds build. Use Lightning Lane (individual or multi-pass) for top-tier rides. Explore Fantasyland — ride Seven Dwarfs Mine Train, Peter Pan's Flight, and 'it's a small world'.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Magic Kingdom. Visit Adventureland for Pirates of the Caribbean and the Jungle Cruise. Catch the Festival of Fantasy Parade (typically 3:00 PM). Take a mid-afternoon break at the hotel if needed (shuttle runs throughout the day) or find air-conditioned refuge inside the park. Return refreshed for the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Magic Kingdom for the evening spectacular — Happily Ever After fireworks show (check My Disney Experience app for exact showtime, typically 9:00 PM). Grab a prime viewing spot on Main Street U.S.A. 30 minutes early. Ride any remaining must-dos after the fireworks when crowds thin. Take the shuttle back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick breakfast at the hotel or a nearby McDonald's/Dunkin' before the shuttle. Budget ~$8–12 per person.
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House in Liberty Square — counter-service seafood and sandwiches. Budget ~$15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: The Plaza Restaurant on Main Street U.S.A. — table-service American classics (burgers, sandwiches, salads). Make an ADV reservation on My Disney Experience. Budget ~$25–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes and bring sunscreen, a refillable water bottle, and a light rain poncho (June afternoons often bring brief Florida thunderstorms). Magic Kingdom is typically the busiest park — arriving at rope drop is critical. Check the My Disney Experience app for real-time wait times throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Disney's Hollywood Studios – Star Wars Experience – Take the hotel shuttle to Hollywood Studios for rope drop (~9:00 AM). Head immediately to Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge. Ride Rise of the Resistance first (use virtual queue or Lightning Lane — book the moment the park opens). Then experience Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run. Explore the immersive land, interact with droids and stormtroopers, and visit Savi's Workshop or the Droid Depot if budget allows (~$120–220 add-on, optional).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the rest of Hollywood Studios. Ride Slinky Dog Dash and Toy Story Mania in Toy Story Land. Catch the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular (check show schedule). Visit Tower of Terror and Rock 'n' Roller Coaster for thrill seekers. Watch the Wonderful World of Animation projection show on the Chinese Theatre facade (evening show, but afternoon rehearsal views are possible).
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the Fantasmic! nighttime spectacular at the Hollywood Hills Amphitheater (typically 8:00 or 9:00 PM — check app). Arrive 45–60 minutes early for good seats. This is one of Disney's best nighttime shows. Take the hotel shuttle back after the show.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at the hotel continental spread or a nearby IHOP on W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy. Budget ~$10–15 per person.
meals.lunch: Docking Bay 7 Food and Cargo in Galaxy's Edge — themed counter-service with creative dishes like Ronto Wraps and Fried Endorian Tip-Yip. Budget ~$15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Sci-Fi Dine-In Theater Restaurant — unique table-service dining inside a mock drive-in theater showing classic sci-fi clips. Make an ADV reservation. Budget ~$25–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Rise of the Resistance is the most in-demand attraction at Walt Disney World — securing Lightning Lane or a virtual queue spot at 7:00 AM (before park open) via the app is essential. Wear layers as some indoor attractions are heavily air-conditioned. Hollywood Studios tends to be very crowded mid-week in June.

day_by_day.morning: Disney's Animal Kingdom – Safari & Avatar Experience – Take the hotel shuttle to Animal Kingdom for rope drop (~8:00 AM; Animal Kingdom often opens early). Head straight to Kilimanjaro Safaris for the best wildlife viewing in the cool morning hours — lions, elephants, giraffes, hippos, and more are most active early. Then explore the Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Pandora – The World of Avatar. Ride Avatar Flight of Passage (Lightning Lane highly recommended — one of the most popular rides in all of Walt Disney World). Experience Na'vi River Journey for a gentler, visually stunning boat ride. Explore the bioluminescent landscape of Pandora. Visit DinoLand U.S.A. for DINOSAUR ride and Primeval Whirl. Catch a live performance at the Theater in the Wild (Finding Nemo: The Big Blue… and Beyond!).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Rivers of Light: We Are One nighttime show at Animal Kingdom (check app for schedule and availability — show times vary). Alternatively, if the show is not running, head back to the hotel for a relaxed evening at the pool. Animal Kingdom typically closes earlier than other parks (~9:00 PM in summer).

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite at Zuri's Sweets Shop or Creature Comforts (Starbucks) near the park entrance upon arrival. Budget ~$8–12 per person.
meals.lunch: Satu'li Canteen in Pandora — counter-service with healthy, flavorful bowls and wraps. One of the best quick-service options in all of Disney World. Budget ~$15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Yak & Yeti Restaurant in Asia — table-service pan-Asian cuisine (Kobe beef, lo mein, ahi tuna). Make an ADV reservation. Budget ~$25–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Animal Kingdom is the most outdoor-heavy park — sunscreen and hydration are critical in June heat. The safari experience is dramatically better in the morning when animals are active. Flight of Passage is widely considered the best ride at Walt Disney World — do not miss it. Check the app for any special character meet-and-greet opportunities.

day_by_day.morning: EPCOT – World Showcase & Food Exploration – Take the hotel shuttle to EPCOT for rope drop (~9:00 AM). Start in Future World (now called World Discovery and World Nature). Ride Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (virtual queue or Lightning Lane — book at 7:00 AM). Experience Test Track and Soarin' Around the World. Visit the stunning aquarium at The Seas with Nemo & Friends.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transition to the World Showcase (opens at 11:00 AM). Walk the 1.2-mile promenade around World Showcase Lagoon, stopping at international pavilions. Sample food and drinks from Mexico (margaritas, tacos), Japan (sushi, mochi), France (crepes, macarons), Morocco, Canada, and more. Visit the Remy's Ratatouille Adventure ride in the France Pavilion. Explore the Mexico Pavilion's indoor Gran Fiesta Tour boat ride.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for EPCOT Forever or Harmonious nighttime spectacular over World Showcase Lagoon (check app for current show name and time — typically 9:00 PM). Find a viewing spot along the lagoon promenade 30–45 minutes early. This is one of Disney's most visually stunning nighttime shows. Take the hotel shuttle back.

meals.breakfast: Sunshine Seasons in The Land Pavilion — counter-service with fresh, healthy options including grain bowls, sandwiches, and pastries. Budget ~$12–18 per person.
meals.lunch: World Showcase food crawl — budget $20–30 per person sampling small plates and snacks across 3–4 pavilions (recommended: La Cantina de San Angel in Mexico, Katsura Grill in Japan, Les Halles Boulangerie-Patisserie in France).
meals.dinner: Teppan Edo in the Japan Pavilion — table-service teppanyaki dining with entertaining chefs. Make an ADV reservation well in advance. Budget ~$35–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT is the largest Disney park by area — comfortable walking shoes are essential. The World Showcase food exploration is a highlight of any Disney trip and aligns perfectly with a balanced, mid-range budget. If traveling with young children, the Kidcot Fun Stops at each pavilion offer free activity sheets. Check for any EPCOT festivals running during your visit (Food & Wine, Flower & Garden, etc.) — June may overlap with a festival offering additional food booths.

day_by_day.morning: Disney Springs Family Entertainment Day – Sleep in and enjoy a relaxed morning. Have a leisurely breakfast at the hotel or a nearby restaurant. Head to Disney Springs mid-morning (~10:00 AM) — no park ticket required, and the hotel shuttle may service Disney Springs (confirm with front desk; otherwise, a rideshare is ~$10–15). Explore the four neighborhoods: The Landing, Marketplace, Town Center, and West Side. Visit the LEGO Store, World of Disney (largest Disney merchandise store in the world), and Art of Disney gallery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy afternoon entertainment at Disney Springs. Visit Splitsville Luxury Lanes for bowling and billiards (great for families, ~$20–25 per person per game). Explore the AMC Disney Springs 24 movie theater if a break from the heat is needed. Browse unique shops and pop-up experiences. Kids can enjoy the interactive water fountain splash pad in the Marketplace area (free). Visit the Coca-Cola Store rooftop for complimentary soda samples from around the world.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner and evening entertainment at Disney Springs. Catch a live music performance at one of the outdoor stages (free, check the Disney Springs entertainment schedule). Browse the evening atmosphere as Disney Springs comes alive with lights and entertainment. Return to the hotel at a relaxed pace — this is a great recovery day before the final park day.

meals.breakfast: Sleep in and enjoy breakfast at the hotel or nearby First Watch (fresh breakfast/brunch restaurant on W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy). Budget ~$12–18 per person.
meals.lunch: D-Luxe Burger at Disney Springs — gourmet burgers with creative toppings in a counter-service setting. Budget ~$15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: The BOATHOUSE at Disney Springs — upscale-casual waterfront dining with fresh seafood, steaks, and classic American fare. Amphicars (vintage amphibious vehicles) offer scenic lake tours. Make an ADV reservation. Budget ~$35–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Disney Springs is free to enter and a wonderful way to experience Disney magic without a park ticket. Saturday is typically the busiest day at Disney Springs — arrive early for parking or use rideshare to avoid the parking garage wait. This day serves as a strategic rest day between park visits, helping to recharge energy for the final park day. The Marketplace Carousel and splash pad are free entertainment for young children.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Favorite Park or Revisit Highlights – Based on the week's experiences, choose your favorite park for a final visit, or use this day to catch any missed attractions. Recommended: Return to Magic Kingdom for any missed rides (Big Thunder Mountain Railroad, Haunted Mansion, Carousel of Progress) or revisit EPCOT for more World Showcase exploration. Alternatively, use this as a flex day to revisit the park your family loved most. Take the hotel shuttle for rope drop one final time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon completing any remaining bucket-list attractions. Visit any character meet-and-greets you may have missed during the week (check My Disney Experience app for character locations and times). Pick up final souvenirs — World of Disney at Disney Springs or park gift shops. If departing later in the week, enjoy the hotel pool for a relaxing final afternoon. Begin packing and preparing for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a local Kissimmee restaurant near the hotel to celebrate a fantastic week. Return to the hotel, complete packing, and arrange departure transportation. Confirm checkout time with the hotel front desk. Reflect on the magical memories made throughout the week.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or grab pastries and coffee at a nearby Panera Bread or Starbucks on W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy. Budget ~$10–15 per person.
meals.lunch: Quick-service meal inside whichever park you visit — budget ~$15–20 per person. Recommended: Pecos Bill Tall Tale Inn and Cafe (Magic Kingdom) or Connections Café (EPCOT).
meals.dinner: Celebration Town Tavern in nearby Celebration, FL (~10 min drive) — casual American dining with a charming small-town Disney-planned community atmosphere. Budget ~$25–40 per person. Alternatively, Taverna Opa on W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy offers lively Greek dining with entertainment. Budget ~$25–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time (typically 11:00 AM) and arrange luggage storage if your departure is later in the day. Many hotels offer bell service to hold bags while you enjoy a final few hours. Confirm return transportation to Orlando International Airport — Mears Connect, rideshare, or rental car return. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Download or screenshot all photos from the My Disney Experience app before your trip ends. Consider purchasing a Disney PhotoPass Memory Maker if you want professional photos from the week.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Disney World, Orlando, Florida Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway - Free Theme Park Shuttle
hotel.location: 7470 W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy, Kissimmee, US (28.3314,-81.5863)

experiences.name: Magic Kingdom Park Adventure
experiences.description: Experience the iconic Magic Kingdom with classic rides like Space Mountain, Pirates of the Caribbean, and the Haunted Mansion. Watch the spectacular Festival of Fantasy parade and end the night with the breathtaking Happily Ever After fireworks show over Cinderella Castle. Perfect for families with children of all ages.
experiences.location: Magic Kingdom, Walt Disney World Resort, Lake Buena Vista

experiences.name: EPCOT World Showcase & Food Exploration
experiences.description: Explore EPCOT's World Showcase featuring 11 international pavilions where you can sample authentic cuisines from countries like Japan, France, Mexico, and Italy. Enjoy cultural performances, artisan demonstrations, and signature rides like Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind and Remy's Ratatouille Adventure. A perfect blend of food, culture, and entertainment.
experiences.location: EPCOT, Walt Disney World Resort, Lake Buena Vista

experiences.name: Disney's Hollywood Studios Star Wars Experience
experiences.description: Immerse your family in the ultimate Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge experience at Disney's Hollywood Studios. Pilot the Millennium Falcon on Smugglers Run, survive the epic Rise of the Resistance ride, and build your own custom lightsaber at Savi's Workshop. Also enjoy Toy Story Land and the thrilling Tower of Terror for a full day of entertainment.
experiences.location: Disney's Hollywood Studios, Walt Disney World Resort, Lake Buena Vista

experiences.name: Disney Springs Family Entertainment Day
experiences.description: Spend a fun-filled day at Disney Springs, Disney World's free-admission entertainment and shopping district just minutes from Kissimmee. Enjoy live street performances, visit the LEGO Store, dine at world-class restaurants like The Boathouse or T-REX Cafe, and catch a movie at the AMC Disney Springs 24 theater. Great for a budget-friendly family day out.
experiences.location: Disney Springs, Walt Disney World Resort, Lake Buena Vista

experiences.name: Disney's Animal Kingdom Safari & Avatar Experience
experiences.description: Embark on the Kilimanjaro Safaris to see real African wildlife including lions, elephants, and giraffes roaming freely. Then journey to Pandora – The World of Avatar for the awe-inspiring Flight of Passage ride and the Na'vi River Journey. End the day with a live Finding Nemo musical show, making it a perfect blend of nature, culture, and family entertainment.
experiences.location: Disney's Animal Kingdom, Walt Disney World Resort, Lake Buena Vista

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight UA arrives at 22:30. No morning or afternoon activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit. Flight arrives late evening.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Orlando International Airport at 22:30. Take the hotel's complimentary theme park shuttle or a pre-booked private car transfer to Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway. Check in, unpack, and settle into your room. Grab a light late-night snack from the hotel's amenities or a nearby 24-hour convenience stop.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport before boarding.
meals.lunch: On the flight or at the airport.
meals.dinner: Late-night arrival – grab a light snack from the hotel vending area, hotel bar if open, or order room service if available. Alternatively, a quick stop at a nearby Denny's or IHOP (open 24 hours, ~5 min drive) to refuel after travel.

day_by_day.notes: Priority on arrival night: check in smoothly, hydrate, and rest. Lay out park essentials (sunscreen, comfortable shoes, ponchos) for an early start tomorrow. Download the My Disney Experience app and confirm all park reservations and Lightning Lane passes in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom Park Adventure – Arrive at rope drop (park opens ~9:00 AM; aim to board the hotel shuttle by 8:00 AM). Start with Tomorrowland: ride Space Mountain and Buzz Lightyear's Space Ranger Spin before crowds build. Use Lightning Lane Multi Pass for top-tier attractions. Head to Fantasyland for Seven Dwarfs Mine Train (book Individual Lightning Lane in advance). Explore Cinderella Castle and catch the early morning character meet-and-greets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue Magic Kingdom exploration through Liberty Square (Haunted Mansion) and Adventureland (Pirates of the Caribbean, Jungle Cruise). Take a mid-afternoon break at a shaded area or the hotel for a quick rest during peak heat (typically 1–3 PM). Return refreshed for the afternoon parade – the Festival of Fantasy parade is a must-see spectacle.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the iconic HAPPILY EVER AFTER fireworks spectacular over Cinderella Castle (typically 9:00 PM). Enjoy the magical light projections and pyrotechnics for a breathtaking end to the day. Depart via the hotel shuttle after the show.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure, or grab a quick bite at Main Street Bakery (Starbucks partner) inside Magic Kingdom upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Be Our Guest Restaurant (Magic Kingdom) – A premium, immersive Beauty and the Beast-themed dining experience inside the Beast's enchanted castle. Reserve in advance via My Disney Experience. Try the French onion soup and braised pork.
meals.dinner: Cinderella's Royal Table – Dine inside Cinderella Castle for a truly magical, upscale experience with character meet-and-greets. Prix-fixe menu featuring premium proteins and elegant desserts. Book 60 days in advance – this is one of Disney's most sought-after reservations.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable, breathable clothing – June in Orlando is hot and humid (highs ~92°F/33°C). Bring a refillable water bottle (free ice water available at any quick-service location). Purchase Lightning Lane Multi Pass and Individual Lightning Lane selections at 7:00 AM sharp via the app.

day_by_day.morning: EPCOT World Showcase & Food Exploration – Arrive at EPCOT for rope drop (~9:00 AM). Begin in Future World (now called World Discovery & World Nature): ride Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (book virtual queue or Individual Lightning Lane immediately upon park open) and Test Track. Explore the stunning new World Celebration area and the Living with the Land boat ride.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transition to the World Showcase as it opens at 11:00 AM. Stroll through all 11 international pavilions – Mexico, Norway (ride Frozen Ever After), China, Germany, Italy, America, Japan, Morocco, France, United Kingdom, and Canada. Sample authentic cuisine and artisan goods from each country. Catch a live cultural performance or film presentation in select pavilions.
day_by_day.evening: Experience EPCOT's HARMONIOUS or the current nighttime spectacular over World Showcase Lagoon – one of the largest nighttime shows ever created for a Disney park, featuring massive floating screens, fountains, and fireworks. Afterward, browse the unique international shops for premium souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Kringla Bakeri og Kafé (Norway Pavilion) – Enjoy traditional Norwegian pastries like school bread and lefse as a mid-morning treat upon World Showcase opening.
meals.lunch: Teppan Edo (Japan Pavilion) – An upscale teppanyaki dining experience with skilled chefs preparing premium meats and seafood tableside. Stunning presentation and authentic flavors.
meals.dinner: Monsieur Paul (France Pavilion) – EPCOT's most refined dining experience, a French haute cuisine restaurant inspired by legendary chef Paul Bocuse. Elegant atmosphere, prix-fixe menu, and an extensive wine list. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT is the most walkable park – wear supportive shoes. The International Food & Wine Festival or Flower & Garden Festival may be running in June – check Disney's event calendar for special kiosks and entertainment. Bring a small crossbody bag for purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Disney's Hollywood Studios – Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Experience – Arrive at rope drop (~9:00 AM). Head directly to Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge. Board Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run first (shorter wait at open). Then experience Rise of the Resistance – one of the most technologically advanced theme park attractions ever built. Explore Black Spire Outpost: build a custom lightsaber at Savi's Workshop (premium experience, ~$250, book in advance) or a custom droid at the Droid Depot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the rest of Hollywood Studios: ride Slinky Dog Dash and Toy Story Mania in Toy Story Land. Experience Tower of Terror and Rock 'n' Roller Coaster Starring Aerosmith in Sunset Boulevard. Catch the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular show (check daily schedule). Take a mid-afternoon break at the hotel if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hollywood Studios for the FANTASMIC! nighttime spectacular – a stunning water, fire, and projection show featuring Mickey Mouse battling Disney villains. Arrive 45–60 minutes early for premium seating. Alternatively, experience the Star Wars: A Galactic Spectacular fireworks show over the park's Chinese Theatre.

meals.breakfast: Woody's Lunch Box (Toy Story Land) – Grab a quick, fun breakfast with totchos or a breakfast bowl before the park gets busy.
meals.lunch: Sci-Fi Dine-In Theater Restaurant – A uniquely themed restaurant where you dine in vintage cars under a simulated starry night sky watching classic sci-fi movie clips. Enjoy premium burgers, sandwiches, and milkshakes in a retro-cool atmosphere.
meals.dinner: The Hollywood Brown Derby – Hollywood Studios' signature fine-dining restaurant inspired by the legendary 1930s Hollywood hotspot. Known for the original Cobb Salad, premium steaks, and an impressive wine selection. Elegant, art-deco ambiance.

day_by_day.notes: Savi's Workshop lightsaber building experience is a premium add-on (~$250 per lightsaber) and requires advance reservations – highly recommended for Star Wars fans of all ages. Wear Star Wars-themed attire for full immersion in Galaxy's Edge.

day_by_day.morning: Disney's Animal Kingdom – Safari & Avatar Experience – Arrive at rope drop (~8:00 AM; Animal Kingdom opens earliest). Head immediately to Pandora – The World of Avatar: ride Avatar Flight of Passage (Individual Lightning Lane strongly recommended – this is the most in-demand ride at Walt Disney World). Then experience Na'vi River Journey for a serene, visually stunning boat ride through a bioluminescent rainforest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board the Kilimanjaro Safaris for a 20-minute open-air safari through 110 acres of authentic African savanna – spot lions, elephants, giraffes, hippos, rhinos, and more. The morning/early afternoon light is ideal for wildlife viewing and photography. Explore the Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail and Maharajah Jungle Trek for up-close animal encounters. Ride Expedition Everest in Asia for a thrilling roller coaster experience.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the Tree of Life Awakenings – as darkness falls, the iconic Tree of Life comes alive with magical insect-inspired projections and storytelling. Catch the Rivers of Light nighttime show if available. Depart for a relaxing evening back at the hotel or head to Disney Springs for after-dinner entertainment.

meals.breakfast: Satu'li Canteen (Pandora – The World of Avatar) – Enjoy a unique, healthy breakfast with grain bowls and protein options in a beautifully themed Avatar environment.
meals.lunch: Tiffins Restaurant (Animal Kingdom) – Disney's most artistically inspired fine-dining restaurant, celebrating the spirit of global exploration. Features rotating menus with globally inspired cuisine, premium proteins, and an exceptional cocktail and wine program. The art throughout the restaurant is stunning.
meals.dinner: Jiko – The Cooking Place (Disney's Animal Kingdom Lodge, ~10 min drive) – One of Walt Disney World's most acclaimed signature restaurants. Features African-inspired cuisine with wood-fired cooking, an award-winning all-African wine list, and a warm, sophisticated atmosphere. A truly world-class dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: Animal Kingdom is best experienced in the early morning when animals are most active and temperatures are cooler. Book Avatar Flight of Passage Individual Lightning Lane at exactly 7:00 AM – it sells out within minutes. The park typically closes earlier than other parks, so plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Disney Springs Family Entertainment Day – Start with a leisurely morning and a late breakfast. Head to Disney Springs (free admission, no park ticket required) when it opens at 10:00 AM. Explore the four neighborhoods: The Landing, Marketplace, Town Center, and West Side. Visit the LEGO Store, World of Disney (largest Disney merchandise store in the world), and unique boutiques. Check out the NBA Experience or Splitsville Luxury Lanes for family fun.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy the vibrant atmosphere of Disney Springs with live entertainment, street performers, and musicians throughout the day. Visit the Marketplace Co-Op for unique, artisan Disney merchandise. Explore the Art of Disney gallery. Take a relaxing boat ride on the waterway if available. Spend time at the AMC Disney Springs 24 if a break from the sun is needed. Optional: book a premium spa treatment at a nearby resort spa for ultimate relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a spectacular dinner at one of Disney Springs' premium restaurants, then take in the lively evening atmosphere with live music and entertainment. The area transforms beautifully at night with lights reflecting off the water. Browse the shops until closing (~11:00 PM on weekends). Return to the hotel via the free shuttle.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a leisurely start at The Polite Pig (Disney Springs) – an upscale craft barbecue restaurant with artisan cocktails and locally sourced ingredients.
meals.lunch: STK Orlando (Disney Springs) – A modern, upscale steakhouse with a vibrant atmosphere. Enjoy premium USDA cuts, fresh seafood, and creative cocktails. One of the most stylish dining experiences at Disney Springs.
meals.dinner: Morimoto Asia (Disney Springs) – Celebrity chef Masaharu Morimoto's flagship pan-Asian restaurant. Features stunning two-story interior, premium sushi, Peking duck, and an extensive sake and cocktail menu. A world-class dining experience in a spectacular setting.

day_by_day.notes: Disney Springs is free to enter and offers free parking (arrive early on weekends as it gets busy). This is a great day to purchase any remaining souvenirs, gifts, or premium Disney merchandise. Consider booking a VIP fireworks cruise on the Seven Seas Lagoon for this evening as a special treat – views of Magic Kingdom fireworks from the water are extraordinary.

day_by_day.morning: Farewell Magic Kingdom or EPCOT Revisit – Depending on checkout time and flight schedule, spend a final morning revisiting your favorite park or any attractions you missed. If returning to Magic Kingdom: catch any missed rides, do final character meet-and-greets, and pick up last-minute Main Street U.S.A. souvenirs. If revisiting EPCOT: explore any remaining World Showcase pavilions and enjoy a final leisurely stroll.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel (standard checkout ~11:00 AM; request late checkout in advance if needed). Store luggage with the hotel concierge if your flight is later in the day. Spend remaining time at Disney Springs for any final shopping or a relaxed lunch. Arrange private car transfer or hotel shuttle to Orlando International Airport with ample time before your departure flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Orlando with magical memories. If your flight is in the evening, enjoy a final premium dinner near the airport or at the airport's dining options in the main terminal.

meals.breakfast: Grand Floridian Café (Disney's Grand Floridian Resort, ~15 min drive) – A beautiful, Victorian-inspired restaurant serving an exceptional breakfast with eggs Benedict, fresh pastries, and premium coffee. A luxurious send-off breakfast.
meals.lunch: Chef Art Smith's Homecomin' (Disney Springs) – Celebrity chef Art Smith's Southern comfort food restaurant featuring fried chicken, hush puppies, and moonshine cocktails. A beloved local favorite with premium ingredients and soulful flavors.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Orlando International Airport (MCO) – Explore the upgraded dining options in the main terminal, or if time allows before heading to the airport, enjoy a final dinner at a nearby premium restaurant in the Kissimmee/Orlando area.

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout (12:00–1:00 PM) from the hotel when checking in to maximize your final morning. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport arrival, security, and boarding at MCO. Consider purchasing a Disney Memory Maker photo package to download all professional Disney PhotoPass photos taken throughout the trip – a wonderful keepsake of your premium Disney World experience.

query: Disney World Orlando family of 4, $6000, 7 days, June
